body: Star Wars Rogue Squadron III: Rebel Strike is Factor 5's GameCube action game expanding the Rebel pilots' campaign beyond aerial combat. Luke Skywalker and Wedge Antilles take part in missions across the original trilogy's setting, with spacecraft joined by ground vehicles and sections on foot. The player moves between different scales of the same conflict. An aircraft can provide a view over the battlefield before another sequence brings attention down to its machinery, soldiers and immediate obstacles, giving the familiar campaign a broader range of physical roles.

The campaign introduces machines such as the AT-ST and speeder bike alongside returning starfighters. Each offers a different relationship to the terrain and opposing forces. The varied sections widen the idea of participating in a Star Wars battle, though their different controls and pace also make the experience less consistent than a campaign built entirely around flight. The strongest aerial encounters retain the series' clear connection between craft and objective, asking the player to recognise what must be protected or destroyed before chasing every enemy visible around it.

A cooperative mode recreates most missions from Rogue Leader for two players sharing a pool of lives. That substantial addition lets familiar operations be approached through coordination, with each person responsible for part of the larger fight. Competitive modes provide other ways to use the available ships. Unlockable Atari Star Wars arcade games connect the collection to earlier adaptations of the same films. Released in 2003, Rebel Strike's most durable expansion may be that opportunity to revisit a memorable flying campaign with another pilot beside the player.
story_headings: Bring a second pilot through Rogue Leader
